methods.label: Identify the overlap
methods.explanation:
Let \(O\) be the square vertex at the circle's center. The two square sides meeting at \(O\) form a \(90^\circ\) angle, and each has length equal to the circle's radius, \(10\).

The overlap is exactly the quarter disk inside this angle. To see why the entire quarter disk fits, note that each of the square's opposite sides is \(10\) units from \(O\). A point at most \(10\) units from \(O\) cannot extend past either opposite side. The rest of the disk lies outside the angle containing the square.

The square has area \(10^2=100\), the disk has area \(\pi\cdot10^2=100\pi\), and their overlap has area \(25\pi\). Adding the two areas counts the overlap twice, so subtract it once:
\[
100+100\pi-25\pi=\boxed{100+75\pi}.
\]
The answer is \(\text{B}\).
